docs.title: DECIMA
docs.text:
Stellar ages, distances and extinctions, with initial [Fe/H], [α/Fe] and evolutionary stage, from spectroscopy plus Gaia and 2MASS photometry. Fast neural posterior estimation on MIST isochrones, then importance sampling that uses every band and the exact parallax likelihood.

You need, for each star: spectroscopic T_eff and [Fe/H] (and [α/Fe], otherwise assumed solar), a Gaia parallax, a Ks magnitude (more bands help), and a sky position.

docs.title: The workflow
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    T[("Your catalogue of observables<br/>FITS, CSV, ...")] --> COLS["<b>decima columns</b><br/>writes the columns file<br/>(your names → DECIMA's)"]
    COLS --> CHECK["<b>decima check</b>"]
    CFG["<b>decima default-config</b><br/>settings file<br/>(optional)"] --> CHECK
    CHECK --> Q{"How many<br/>stars?"}
    Q -- "up to a few thousand" --> INF["<b>decima.infer</b><br/>in Python"]
    Q -- "more, or a long job" --> RUN["<b>decima run</b> --out run/<br/>chunks, workers, resumable"]
    INF --> OUT["summary · samples · rejected"]
    RUN --> OUT
    OUT --> FILT["drop <code>failed</code> stars,<br/>look at <code>ess_frac</code>"]

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/teresa-su/decima && cd decima
uv sync                 # or: pip install -e .

uv sync creates the environment in decima/.venv. Activate it so that decima and python find the install (or skip activating and prefix commands with uv run):

source .venv/bin/activate

To use DECIMA in Jupyter, install the notebook extras and register the environment as a kernel (or, in VS Code, choose .venv/bin/python as the interpreter):

uv sync --group dev
python -m ipykernel install --user --name decima

Python ≥ 3.10. The trained models (doi:10.5281/zenodo.24584265, CC-BY-4.0, 245 MB) are downloaded from Zenodo the first time DECIMA needs them and cached (~/.cache/decima/v1 on Linux). If your compute nodes have no internet, run decima download-models on the login node first. To keep the models elsewhere, or use a copy you already have, set DECIMA_DATA_DIR to that directory.

docs.title: Tutorial: from a catalogue to ages¶
docs.text:
This is a short tutorial to show how to infer ages, distances and extinctions for a handful of stars. It also shows how to identify when the pipeline has failed/produced unreliable results.

Step 1 Look at your table 2 Make the columns file: your column names → DECIMA's 3 Check everything before running 4 Choose the settings 5 Run 6 Read the summary, the samples and the rejected stars 7 Spot a star you should not trust

docs.title: Install¶
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/teresa-su/decima && cd decima
uv sync --group dev        # or: pip install -e .

uv sync creates the environment in decima/.venv. To run this notebook in it, register it as a Jupyter kernel and select the decima kernel (in VS Code, choose .venv/bin/python as the interpreter instead):

source .venv/bin/activate
python -m ipykernel install --user --name decima

The first time DECIMA runs inference it downloads the trained models (doi:10.5281/zenodo.24584265, CC-BY-4.0, 245 MB) from Zenodo and caches them (~/.cache/decima/v1 on Linux). If your compute nodes have no internet, run decima download-models on the login node first. To keep the models elsewhere, or use a copy you already have, set DECIMA_DATA_DIR to that directory.

docs.title: 1. Look at your table¶
docs.text: data/example_stars.ecsv has seven stars with spectroscopy (LAMOST-style names), Gaia and 2MASS photometry. Five are real stars from the Xiang+24 catalogue. Two are copies altered for this tutorial: one has no T_eff, and one has a parallax that does not fit its spectroscopy. DECIMA reads any table astropy reads (FITS, CSV, ECSV, ...) and also pandas data frames.

docs.title: 2. Make the columns file¶
docs.text:
DECIMA has its own names for the columns it needs (teff, feh, parallax, Ks, ... see the input reference). If your table calls them something else, the columns file will provide the mapping: DECIMA's name → table name.

You do not have to write it by hand. suggest_columns (on the shell: decima columns stars.ecsv -o cols.json) matches names for you:

docs.title: 3. Check before you run¶
docs.text: check_inputs (shell: decima check stars.ecsv --columns cols.json) reads your table and the columns file and reports what would go wrong, including values that look like the wrong unit (log T_eff instead of K, parallax in arcsec, 99 as a "missing" magnitude).

docs.title: 4. Choose the settings¶
docs.text: Everything that changes the result is in decima.Config; the defaults are the ones DECIMA was validated with. The settings file is a different file from the columns file: it holds these settings, not column names. Change what you need and leave the rest:

docs.title: 6. Read the results¶
docs.text: summary has one row per star that was run. For every quantity it has percentiles (5, 16, 50, 84, 95): age_p16, age_p50, age_p84 give the median age and a 68% interval, in Gyr.

docs.title: 7. Spot a star you should not trust¶
docs.text: failed flags stars with no usable result. None failed here. But a star can come out without being flagged and still be doubtful. ess_frac is the effective sample size of the final weights as a fraction of the draws DECIMA made. A small value means the photometry and parallax disagree with what the spectroscopy predicts.

docs.title: Extinction laws
docs.text:
For every stage-1 draw, stage 2 fits a distance modulus μ and one extinction value E to the apparent magnitudes:

m_b − M_b(θ) = μ + R_b E

The extinction law supplies R_b, the extinction in band b per unit E.

Kind of law E is Output column Fixed laws E(B−V) ebv Colour-dependent laws A0, the monochromatic extinction at 550 nm A0

Choose a law with Config(extinction=...).

docs.title: Built-in laws
docs.text: Name Kind E Source F19 (default) colour-dependent, X = (BP−RP)₀ A0 Gaia EDR3 extinction coefficients for the Fitzpatrick+19 curve ("top of the HRD" fit) F19_TEFF colour-dependent, X = T_eff / 5040 K A0 the same, as a function of T_eff SS2018 fixed E(B−V) Schlafly & Finkbeiner (2018)-type R_b WC2019 fixed E(B−V) Wang & Chen (2019) none R_b = 0 — No extinction: stage 2 fits the distance alone, and gives no extinction estimate. For mock stars.

docs.title: Colour-dependent laws
docs.text:
A fixed law uses one R_b per band for every star. A colour-dependent law gives each band a coefficient

k_b = A_b / A0 = c₀ + c₁X + c₂X² + c₃X³ + c₄A + c₅A² + c₆A³ + c₇XA + c₈AX² + c₉XA²

where A = A0, and X is the intrinsic colour (or T_eff) of the draw being weighted, taken from the noise-free isochrone. Since k_b depends on A0, the value being fitted, stage 2 fits once with k_b at A0 = 0, then refits once with k_b at the fitted A0.

Two clamps keep the polynomial inside its calibration, so it is never extrapolated: - X is clamped to the fit's range: (BP−RP)₀ ∈ [−0.06, 2.5] for F19, and T_eff ∈ [3500, 10000] K for F19_TEFF. - A0 is clamped to [0, 20].

The summary column frac_colour_clipped is the fraction of a star's draws whose X was clamped. A value near 1 means the star is outside the law's calibrated colours.

To convert, E(B−V) = A0 / 3.1.

docs.title: Grey component
docs.text: Config(grey=0.1) adds a grey extinction component of 0.1 to every R_b of a built-in law.

docs.title: Your own law
docs.text:
Constant R_b per band:

import decima

law = decima.FixedLaw({"G": 2.29, "BP": 3.05, "RP": 1.74, "J": 0.63, "H": 0.32, "Ks": 0.16})
cfg = decima.Config(extinction=law)

A Fitzpatrick+19-form polynomial with your own coefficients: ten per band, in the order decima.extinction.POLY_TERMS, with X either "BP-RP" or "teff":

law = decima.PolynomialLaw(coeffs, x="BP-RP", x_range=(-0.06, 2.5), a0_max=20.0, r_v=3.1)

FixedLaw and PolynomialLaw are saved in config.json, so a run that uses them can be resumed and reproduced.

Anything else: subclass decima.ExtinctionLaw. Set bands, colour_dependent, extinction_name and columns (the isochrone columns you need), and implement __call__. Its contract is in the docstring of decima/extinction.py. Define to_dict as well if runs using the law should be reproducible from config.json.

A law must have coefficients for every band in Config.bands.

docs.title: How DECIMA works
docs.text:
DECIMA infers θ = ([Fe/H]_init, [α/Fe]_init, log age, EEP) for each star, plus its distance and extinction. θ lives on a grid of MIST v2.5 isochrones (v/v_crit = 0.4). Two neural posterior estimators (NPEs) and one density estimator, all trained on simulations from that grid, give a first posterior over θ. Importance sampling then refines it with the photometry and parallax, and adds the posteriors over distance and extinction.

The details, derivations and validation are in the DECIMA paper (in preparation). This page is the short version.

docs.title: The pipeline at a glance
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    IN["Per star: spectroscopy s = ([Fe/H], [α/Fe], log T<sub>eff</sub>)<br/>Ks and parallax → pseudo-magnitude M<sub>pseudo,K</sub><br/>magnitudes m<sub>b</sub>, parallax ϖ, optional log g"]

    subgraph S1["Stage 1: distance-independent, neural posterior estimation"]
        direction TB
        A["1. Draw n_latent_x noise-free spectroscopic observables s′<br/>around the measured s, weighted by q(s′)"]
        B["2. For each s′ draw n_theta values of θ from a defensive mixture<br/>mixture_alpha: q(θ | s′, M<sub>pseudo,K</sub>) · rest: q(θ | s′)"]
        C["3. Stage-1 weight: q(s′) · q(θ | s′) / mixture proposal<br/>(the parallax is counted once, in stage 2)"]
        A --> B --> C
    end

    subgraph S2["Stage 2: importance sampling with the photometry and parallax"]
        direction TB
        D["4. Isochrone lookup: absolute magnitudes M<sub>b</sub>(θ) of every draw"]
        E["5. Fit distance modulus μ and extinction E to m<sub>b</sub> − M<sub>b</sub><br/>(weighted least squares; the parallax joins when precise)"]
        F["6. Draw (μ, E) around the fit with E ≥ 0; convert μ to distance d"]
        G["7. Stage-2 weight: photometric and parallax likelihoods,<br/>IMF and distance priors, (log g) / proposal density"]
        D --> E --> F --> G
    end

    OUT["8. Multiply the weights and resample (θ, d, E):<br/>unweighted posterior samples, percentiles and diagnostics"]
    IN --> A
    C --> D
    G --> OUT

Settings that act on each step are named in the settings reference.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
Symbol What s = ([Fe/H], [α/Fe], log T_eff) spectroscopic surface observables M_pseudo,K = ϖ · 10^(0.2 Ks − 2) the pseudo absolute magnitude (parallax ϖ in mas), equal to 10^(−0.2 M_Ks) for a star without extinction m_b, b ∈ {G, BP, RP, J, H, Ks} apparent magnitudes ϖ parallax log g optional (use_logg)

The spectroscopy and M_pseudo,K are distance-independent; the magnitudes and parallax are not.

docs.title: The trained models
docs.text:
Model What it is q(θ | s, M_pseudo,K) NPE conditioned on the spectroscopy and the pseudo absolute magnitude q(θ | s) NPE conditioned on the spectroscopy only q(s) density of the spectroscopic observables under the training prior

All three were trained with sbi on 70,000 noise-free simulations drawn uniformly over the grid. The NPEs work in a transformed θ, rescaled to the grid range and logit-transformed (decima.theta). DECIMA converts their draws back to physical θ.

docs.title: Stage 1: spectroscopic posterior
docs.text:
Measurement noise is handled at inference time, not in the networks: 1. For each star, DECIMA draws n_latent_x noise-free versions of the observables around the measured ones, and weights each by q(s). 2. For each of these, it draws n_theta values of θ from a defensive mixture: a fraction mixture_alpha (0.1) from the luminosity-informed q(θ | s, M_pseudo,K), the rest from q(θ | s).

The mixture concentrates draws where the parallax will put the star, while still covering the tails of the posterior.

docs.title: Stage 2: photometry and parallax
docs.text:
For every stage-1 draw, the isochrone gives the absolute magnitudes: 1. DECIMA fits a distance modulus and an extinction E to the observed magnitudes, and draws (d, E) around the fit, with E ≥ 0. 2. Each draw is weighted by the photometric likelihood, the parallax likelihood, the distance prior, the IMF prior and, optionally, the log g likelihood. 3. The draws are resampled in proportion to their weights.

The weights also swap the proposal for q(θ | s), so the parallax is counted once.

docs.title: Priors
docs.text:
The trained models are deliberately kept free of physical priors: they see θ drawn uniformly over the grid. Priors are applied afterwards, as importance weights in stage 2. DECIMA currently has the ability to apply the IMF prior on θ and a distance prior; support for user-defined priors is planned.

On Prior θ uniform over the grid in training; the IMF (Kroupa 2001) is applied in stage 2 (imf_prior) distance Bailer-Jones+21 generalised gamma, with parameters from the star's HEALPix pixel (per-star L, alpha, beta override the map) extinction flat, E ≥ 0

docs.text: On by default. Config(pseudo_mag_inflate=False) turns it off.

docs.title: The problem
docs.text:
Stage 1 conditions the main NPE on the pseudo absolute magnitude

M_pseudo,K = ϖ · 10^(0.2 Ks − 2) = 10^(−0.2 (M_Ks − A_Ks))

The NPE was trained without extinction, so it reads M_pseudo,K as if A_Ks = 0. For a reddened star, M_pseudo,K is then 10^(0.2 A_Ks) times too large, and the star looks more luminous than it is.

Stage 2 fits the extinction and would correct this, but only by reweighting the stage-1 draws. If stage 1's proposal is centred on the wrong luminosity and is narrow, few draws land where stage 2 wants them. Stage 2 then rests on a handful of draws: low ess_frac, and noisy, sometimes biased results.

docs.title: What pseudo_mag_inflate does
docs.text:
1. Estimate A_K cheaply from data already in the input.
  2. The Casagrande+21 colour–T_eff relation for Gaia EDR3 BP and 2MASS Ks (their Table A1, (BP−Ks)₀) gives T_eff = f((BP−Ks)₀, log g, [Fe/H]).
  3. Inverting it at the star's spectroscopic T_eff, log g and [Fe/H] gives the intrinsic colour (BP−Ks)₀, so E(BP−Ks) = (BP−Ks)_obs − (BP−Ks)₀.
  4. Then A_K = 0.124 · E(BP−Ks), clipped at 0.
  5. This needs no dust map and no external E(B−V).

  6. Widen, don't correct. The M_pseudo,K error is increased in quadrature by the fraction of M_pseudo,K the extinction could account for:

    σ² → σ² + (0.2 ln 10 · M_pseudo,K · A_K)²

The value of M_pseudo,K is left alone. Stage 2 still does the actual extinction fit, with all bands. The inflation only makes the stage-1 proposal wide enough for stage 2 to work with.

The estimate is noisy: σ(A_K) ≈ 0.006 mag from star to star on Xiang+24. That is small next to the A_K of the stars where the inflation matters, but not next to the median (≈0.017). This noise is why the estimate is used only to widen the error, never to correct M_pseudo,K.

docs.title: When it applies
docs.text:
A star's error is inflated (pseudo_mag_inflated = True in the summary) only when all of these hold: - BP and Ks are both present. - BP > 5 and G > 6 (brighter stars are saturated in Gaia). - The relation has a solution with (BP−Ks)₀ in [0.30, 4.20] that reproduces the star's T_eff to within 1 K. In practice this means 4000 K ≲ T_eff ≲ 8000 K, the calibrated range.

Otherwise the error is left as it was, and the star runs normally.

docs.title: Reference
docs.text: Casagrande, L. et al. 2021, MNRAS 507, 2684: The GALAH survey: effective temperature calibration from the InfraRed Flux Method in the Gaia system.

docs.title: Make your columns file and settings file¶
docs.text:
A DECIMA run is steered by two small JSON files. They are different things, and mixing them up is the commonest early mistake:

Columns file Settings file Answers Which of my columns is which? How should DECIMA compute? Content DECIMA's column name → your column name Every setting in decima.Config Example {"teff": "TEFF", "Ks": "ks_m"} {"n_keep": 1000, "extinction": "F19"} Make it decima columns stars.fits -o cols.json decima default-config > settings.json Pass it --columns cols.json or columns={...} --config settings.json or config=Config(...) Needed? Unless your table already uses DECIMA's names No: the defaults are the validated ones

This page needs no models. It uses the example table from the tutorial.

docs.title: 1. Let DECIMA suggest the columns file¶
docs.text: suggest_columns compares your column names with the usual names for each input: Gaia archive names, E_X / X_err / X_error error columns, *_msigcom for 2MASS, and so on. Case and punctuation are ignored.

docs.title: 2. When the suggestion is not enough¶
docs.text: DECIMA never guesses between two candidates. Here a table has two T_eff columns, and no column that looks like [Fe/H]:

docs.title: 3. Check the table, the columns file and the settings together¶
docs.text: check_inputs (shell: decima check stars.fits --columns cols.json --config settings.json) is the step that saves hours. It reads your data and tells you what would go wrong. Here is a table with four planted mistakes (and one renamed column, which we map by hand):

docs.title: 4. The settings file¶
docs.text: decima default-config prints the defaults. Save them, change what you want, keep the rest:

docs.title: 5. Use them¶
docs.text:
decima check stars.fits --columns cols.json --config settings.json
decima run   stars.fits --columns cols.json --config settings.json --out run/

or in Python, decima.infer("stars.fits", columns, cfg). The tutorial does this end to end, and Run a large catalogue covers decima run.

docs.title: Common problems¶
docs.text: | You see | Cause and fix | |---|---| | required column teff is missing; 'TEFF' looks right | The table's name differs from DECIMA's: add "teff": "TEFF" to the columns file, or run decima columns. | | unknown canonical column ... did you mean 'teff' | The columns file has the keys the wrong way round or misspelt: the key is DECIMA's name, the value is yours. | | column(s) not in the table: teff -> 'TEF' | The value is not a column of your table. Names are case-sensitive. | | teff: median 3.77 ... Kelvin | The column holds log₁₀ T_eff. Convert it to K in your table. | | Ks: 1 value(s) > 30 mag | A flag such as 99 for "not measured". Replace it with NaN. | | parallax: 90% of |values| are below 0.02 | Parallax is in arcseconds. DECIMA wants mas. | | unknown setting 'n_thetas' | A misspelt setting in the settings file; the message lists the valid ones. |

docs.title: Run a large catalogue
docs.text: Use decima.infer for up to a few thousand stars in a notebook (tutorial). For anything bigger use decima run: it works through the catalogue in chunks, saves each chunk as it finishes, spreads them over worker processes, and resumes if it is interrupted.

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
decima check catalogue.fits --columns cols.json --config settings.json     # first: catches mistakes in seconds
decima run catalogue.fits --out run/ --columns cols.json --config settings.json --workers 16

The same from Python:

import decima

if __name__ == "__main__":      # needed in a script: workers are started as fresh processes
    decima.run("catalogue.fits", out="run/", columns=cols, config=cfg, workers=16)

--columns is the columns file (your names → DECIMA's) and --config the settings file; both are optional.

Option Default Description --workers 1 Worker processes. Each uses one CPU thread and loads its own copy of the models (about 0.25 GB). --chunk 250 Stars per checkpoint. Also sets the random draws (below). --format fits Format of the summary table: any extension astropy writes (ecsv, csv, …).

docs.title: If it stops: run the same command again
docs.text:
If the run stops for any reason without finishing: run the same command again. Finished chunks are skipped and the rest are done. Two things are checked first:

  • the settings and --chunk must be the same, or the run is refused (holds a run with different settings); start a new --out instead;
  • DECIMA does not check that the table and columns file are the same as before. Keep them unchanged.

If some chunks fail (look at progress.log for the error), the run ends with N chunk(s) failed or are missing. Fix the cause and run the same command again to retry only those.

docs.title: What is in the run directory
docs.text:
File Contents summary.fits One row per star that was run: percentiles, failed, ess_frac, … (columns) samples.h5 samples (n_stars, n_keep, 7), id, quantity_names rejected.ecsv Rows that could not be run, and why config.json, job.json The settings and chunk size of this run progress.log A line per finished or failed chunk, with timings inputs.pt, chunk_XXXXXX.npz Working files that make resuming possible. Delete them when the run is finished.

Rejected stars are not in the summary, so its rows do not line up with your table's. Map an id column and match on it.

docs.title: Reproducible results
docs.text: Chunk c is seeded seed + c × chunk, so results do not depend on the number of workers, but they do depend on --chunk. decima.infer(..., chunk=250) gives the same draws as decima run with the same --chunk.

docs.title: GPU
docs.text:
Put "device": "cuda" in the settings file (or cuda:1 for a particular GPU):

decima default-config | sed 's/"cpu"/"cuda"/' > settings.json
  • Lower stars_per_batch (default 100) if GPU memory runs out.
  • CUDA and CPU draw different random numbers, so their results differ within the posterior's noise.

docs.title: Decide which results to trust
docs.text: DECIMA returns a posterior for every star it can run, including stars where something is wrong. Four things to look at before using a result.

docs.title: 1. Drop failed stars
docs.text:
failed = True means the star's result is not usable: either no stage-1 draw was usable (its percentiles are NaN), or its age posterior has no width on one side of the median, because a few draws carry all the weight. uniform_fallback = True means every weight vanished and the "posterior" is just the proposal: treat it as failed too.

good = ~summary["failed"] & ~summary["uniform_fallback"]

On the Xiang+24 catalogue (≈250,000 stars) 0.1% of stars failed.

docs.title: 2. Look at the effective sample size
docs.text:
ess_frac is the effective sample size of the final importance weights as a fraction of the n_latent_x × n_theta draws. The effective sample size is roughly the number of independent posterior draws behind the percentiles:

cfg = decima.Config()
summary["ess"] = summary["ess_frac"] * cfg.n_latent_x * cfg.n_theta

A low value means the photometry and parallax disagree with what the spectroscopy predicts. There is no calibrated cut-off. In the tests behind pseudo_mag_inflate ess_frac < 0.01 was the level counted as low, so a sensible first step is to look at those stars one by one rather than cutting blindly. Typical causes:

  • an unresolved binary (not modelled by DECIMA);
  • a bad magnitude, or a bad parallax;
  • a T_eff or [Fe/H] that is wrong or on a different scale from the models;
  • high extinction.

The tutorial shows one such star.

docs.title: 3. Check what went into each star
docs.text: Columns Look for G_used, BP_used, … Bands that were skipped for the star (no magnitude, or no error). Fewer bands means a weaker constraint on distance and extinction. G_err_missing, … The magnitude had no error, so missing_err (0.5 mag by default) was used. par_valid The parallax was precise enough to enter the distance-extinction fit directly. pseudo_mag_inflated The pseudo-magnitude error was widened for possible extinction. zero_point_applied The parallax zero-point was subtracted. ess_norm_stage1 Low when the spectroscopy sits at the edge of the training prior.

docs.title: 4. Check the star is inside what DECIMA was validated on
docs.text:
DECIMA runs on any star from the main sequence to the end of the horizontal branch, but it was tested on a limited domain:

Trained on [Fe/H] −4 to +0.5; [α/Fe] −0.2 to +0.6; age up to 20 Gyr; from the ZAMS to the end of core-He burning (main sequence to horizontal branch) Tested on real stars Xiang+24 turn-off and subgiant stars (T_eff ≈ 5000–6650 K, log g ≈ 3.35–4.3, [Fe/H] ≈ −1.7 to +0.3): residuals against catalogue ages have mean +0.2 Gyr and RMS 1.05 Gyr Not modelled Unresolved binaries. These will have underestimated ages.

docs.title: decima.infer(source, columns=None, config=None, models=None, chunk=250)
docs.text:
Run DECIMA in memory on a table (path, astropy Table or pandas DataFrame); for big catalogs use decima.run.

Returns (summary, samples, rejected): the per-star astropy Table, the (n_stars, n_keep, n_q) posterior samples (columns quantity_names(config)) and a Table of the input rows that could not be run, with the reason. Chunk c of chunk stars is seeded config.seed + c * chunk, as in decima.run, so both give the same draws.

docs.title: decima.run(source, out, columns=None, config=None, workers=1, chunk=250, summary_format='fits')
docs.text: Run DECIMA on source (path, astropy Table or pandas DataFrame) into the directory out; see the module docstring. summary_format is the file extension astropy writes the summary table with (fits, ecsv, csv, ...). Returns the path of the summary table.

docs.title: decima.Config dataclass
docs.text: Every setting that changes the result. Saved as config.json next to a run's output.

docs.title: from_json(text) classmethod
docs.text: Settings from the text of a settings file (decima default-config > settings.json). Missing settings keep their defaults.

docs.title: decima.suggest_columns(source)
docs.text:
Suggest the columns file for a table: which of its columns hold DECIMA's inputs.

Matches column names ignoring case and punctuation against the usual names (COLUMN_INFO): Gaia archive names, E_X / X_ERR / X_error error columns, *_msigcom for 2MASS, and so on. When two columns could both be x, nothing is guessed: the candidates are in .ambiguous. Check the result (units, in particular): decima.check_inputs.

docs.title: decima.check_inputs(source, columns=None, config=None)
docs.text:
Check a table, a columns file and settings before a run. Needs no models.

source: path, astropy Table or pandas DataFrame. columns: the columns mapping (canonical -> yours) or None. config: a Config, the path of a settings file, or None for the defaults. Reports missing or misnamed columns, values that look like the wrong unit, and how many stars would be rejected (a dry run of build_inputs).

docs.title: decima.quantity_names(cfg)
docs.text: Columns of the saved samples: theta, age [Gyr], distance [pc] and the fitted extinction (A0 or ebv).

docs.title: Input columns
docs.text:
DECIMA reads any table astropy reads (FITS, CSV, ECSV, VOTable, HDF5, Parquet), or an astropy Table or pandas DataFrame. It looks for the column names below. If your table uses other names, map them with a columns file (decima columns writes one for you, see Make your columns file); the file maps DECIMA's name → your name.

{"teff": "TEFF", "teff_error": "e_teff", "Ks": "ks_m"}

Names are case-sensitive: Ks, not ks. Use NaN (or a masked value) for anything not measured, not a flag such as -9999 or 99: decima check warns about those.

docs.title: Required
docs.text: Column Unit Meaning parallax mas Gaia parallax (zero-point corrected, or see parallax_zero_point). parallax_error mas Uncertainty on parallax. teff K Spectroscopic effective temperature. teff_error K Uncertainty on T_eff. Used as given (no floor). feh dex Spectroscopic surface [Fe/H]. feh_error dex Uncertainty on [Fe/H]. Used as given (no floor). Ks mag 2MASS Ks apparent magnitude (required: it gives the pseudo-magnitude). Ks_error mag Uncertainty on 2MASS Ks, floored at twomass_err_floor; a magnitude without one gets missing_err.

docs.title: Position (ra and dec, or L, alpha and beta)
docs.text: Column Unit Meaning ra deg Right ascension (ICRS), for the Bailer-Jones+21 distance prior. dec deg Declination (ICRS), for the Bailer-Jones+21 distance prior. L pc Per-star Bailer-Jones+21 prior length scale; with alpha and beta it replaces the lookup from ra, dec. alpha Per-star Bailer-Jones+21 prior shape parameter (with L, beta). beta Per-star Bailer-Jones+21 prior shape parameter (with L, alpha).

docs.title: Optional
docs.text: Column Unit Meaning id Star identifier. Without it the summary's id is the 0-based row of the input table. alpha_fe dex Spectroscopic [alpha/Fe]. Missing values are filled with alpha_fe_fill (default 0) +- alpha_fe_err_fill (default 0.2). alpha_fe_error dex Uncertainty on [alpha/Fe]. Used as given (no floor). logg dex Spectroscopic log g (cgs). Used for the pseudo-magnitude inflation, and in stage 2 only with use_logg. logg_error dex Uncertainty on log g. G mag Gaia G apparent magnitude. NaN or masked: the band is skipped for that star. BP mag Gaia BP apparent magnitude. NaN or masked: the band is skipped for that star. RP mag Gaia RP apparent magnitude. NaN or masked: the band is skipped for that star. J mag 2MASS J apparent magnitude. NaN or masked: the band is skipped for that star. H mag 2MASS H apparent magnitude. NaN or masked: the band is skipped for that star. G_error mag Uncertainty on Gaia G, floored at gaia_err_floor; a magnitude without one gets missing_err. BP_error mag Uncertainty on Gaia BP, floored at gaia_err_floor; a magnitude without one gets missing_err. RP_error mag Uncertainty on Gaia RP, floored at gaia_err_floor; a magnitude without one gets missing_err. J_error mag Uncertainty on 2MASS J, floored at twomass_err_floor; a magnitude without one gets missing_err. H_error mag Uncertainty on 2MASS H, floored at twomass_err_floor; a magnitude without one gets missing_err.

docs.title: Parallax zero-point (only with parallax_zero_point=True)
docs.text: Column Unit Meaning nu_eff_used_in_astrometry 1/um Gaia archive column; only for parallax_zero_point (which also needs G). pseudocolour 1/um Gaia archive column; only for parallax_zero_point. ecl_lat deg Gaia archive column (ecliptic latitude); only for parallax_zero_point. astrometric_params_solved Gaia archive column (31 = 5-parameter, 95 = 6-parameter solution); only for parallax_zero_point.

docs.title: Missing values and rejected stars
docs.text:
• Missing magnitude: NaN or masked. That band is skipped for that star.
  • Magnitude without an error: gets the error missing_err (0.5 mag by default; 0 uses the error floor instead).
  • Error floors: G, BP, RP errors are floored at gaia_err_floor, J, H, Ks at twomass_err_floor. Spectroscopic errors are used as given.
  • Missing [α/Fe] (or its error): filled with alpha_fe_fill ± alpha_fe_err_fill (0 ± 0.2 by default).
  • Rejected stars: a star is not run, and is listed in rejected with the reason, if it has no value for a required column (no teff, no Ks, …), parallax_error <= 0, or no position (no ra, dec (or L, alpha, beta)). Only the first reason is recorded. Negative parallaxes are allowed.
  • Row numbers: rejected stars are left out of the summary, so its rows do not line up with the input rows. Map an id column to match them up; without one, the summary's id is the 0-based input row.

docs.title: Parallax
docs.text: Used as given, or with parallax_zero_point=True DECIMA subtracts the Lindegren+21 zero-point itself (details). Give DECIMA one or the other: do not correct a parallax twice.

docs.title: Outputs, and how to tell a good result from a bad one
What you get
docs.text:
decima.infer returns three things: - summary: an astropy Table, one row per star that was run, in input order; - samples: a numpy array of shape (n_stars, n_keep, 7); - rejected: a Table of the input rows that could not be run.

decima.run / decima run writes a directory:

File Contents summary.<format> The summary table (default FITS) samples.h5 samples (n_stars, n_keep, 7) float32, id (n_stars,), quantity_names (7,) rejected.ecsv Input rows that could not be run: row, id (if given), reason config.json, job.json The settings and chunk size of the run progress.log One line per finished or failed chunk, with timings inputs.pt, chunk_XXXXXX.npz Intermediate files, kept so the run can resume. Delete them once the run has finished.

docs.title: The quantities
docs.text:
The seven columns of samples, in order (decima.quantity_names(cfg)):

Name Unit feh_init dex initial [Fe/H] of the model star. The present-day surface value is what you input. alpha_fe_init dex initial [α/Fe] log_age log₁₀(yr) eep — MIST equivalent evolutionary point: 202 ZAMS, 454 TAMS, 605 RGB tip, 631 ZACHeB, 707 end of core-He burning age Gyr 10^(log_age − 9) distance pc A0 or ebv mag A0 for the colour-dependent laws (F19, F19_TEFF); E(B−V) for fixed laws. See Extinction laws.

The samples are unweighted draws from the posterior. They were resampled from the n_latent_x × n_theta importance-weighted draws, so some appear more than once. They are already in random order, so the first k of them are a valid smaller sample.

docs.title: The summary table
docs.text:
id comes from the input id column, or is the 0-based input row. Then, for each quantity above and each of Config.percentiles (5, 16, 50, 84, 95), a column <quantity>_p<P>, such as age_p50 or distance_p16. Then the diagnostics and flags:

Column Meaning failed The star failed: no usable stage-1 draw, or an age posterior with no width on one side of the median. Do not use its results. uniform_fallback Every importance weight vanished, so the 'posterior' is just the stage-1 proposal. Treat as failed. ess_frac Effective sample size of the stage-2 importance weights as a fraction of the stage-1 draws. The main quality number. ess_norm_stage1 Effective sample size of the stage-1 q(s) weights as a fraction of the draws. Low when the spectroscopy sits at the edge of the training prior. frac_valid_samples_pre Fraction of stage-1 draws usable in stage 2: on the grid, with enough bands, and a finite weight. frac_colour_clipped Fraction of draws whose intrinsic colour was outside the extinction law's calibration (colour-dependent laws only). n_negative_extinction Number of draws whose sampled extinction was negative or NaN, and which were dropped. par_valid The parallax was precise enough (parallax_snr_min) to enter the stage-2 distance-extinction fit directly. The exact parallax likelihood is used either way. pseudo_mag_inflated The pseudo absolute magnitude error was widened by an A_K estimate (pseudo_mag_inflate). zero_point_applied The Lindegren+21 parallax zero-point was subtracted from this star's parallax (parallax_zero_point). {band}_used The band had a magnitude and an error for this star, so it entered stage 2. {band}_err_missing The band had a magnitude but no error, so missing_err was used.

The table's header (FITS) or meta (ECSV) records the DECIMA version (DECIMA), the model release (MODELS) and the full config (CONFIG, as JSON).

docs.title: When to distrust a star
docs.text:
Failed stars (failed = True): - either no stage-1 draw was usable at all, and its percentiles and samples are NaN; - or its age posterior has no width on one side of the median: the 16th or the 84th percentile equals the median. This happens when a few draws carry all the weight.

On the Xiang+24 catalogue, 0.1% of stars failed.

Low effective sample size. ESS = ess_frac × n_latent_x × n_theta is roughly the number of independent posterior draws behind a star's result. A low ESS means the photometry and parallax disagree with what the spectroscopy predicts, so look at those stars before using them. Typical causes: - a binary; - a bad magnitude; - a T_eff or [Fe/H] that is wrong, or on a different scale from the models; - high extinction.

docs.title: Resuming and re-running
docs.text: Re-running the same decima run command into the same directory skips finished chunks and retries failed ones. A different config or chunk size is refused. Use a new directory instead. Results do not depend on the number of workers, and decima.infer with the same chunk gives the same draws as decima.run.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Every setting that can change a result lives in decima.Config. In a run they come from the settings file, which is a different file from the columns file.

PythonShell 
cfg = decima.Config(bands=("BP", "RP", "J", "H", "Ks"), gaia_err_floor=0.03)

decima default-config > settings.json     # write the defaults, edit what you want to change
decima run stars.fits --out run/ --config settings.json

A settings file needs only the settings you change; the rest keep their defaults. A misspelt name or an impossible value is reported before anything runs (decima check does the same without starting a run).

A run directory keeps its config.json. Running into the same directory with different settings is refused, so the outputs always match the settings stored next to them. The summary file also records the settings, the DECIMA version and the model release in its header (FITS) or meta (ECSV).

Defaults are shown as they appear in the settings file (JSON: true, not True).

docs.title: Sampling
docs.text: Setting Default What it does n_latent_x 800 Latent (noise-free) observables drawn per star in stage 1: the Monte Carlo sample over the observational noise n_theta 10 Theta draws per latent observable n_keep 400 Posterior samples kept per star (of n_latent_x * n_theta) percentiles [5, 16, 50, 84, 95] Percentiles written to the summary table seed 22 Random seed for every draw (latent observables, theta, distance and extinction): the same inputs and seed give the same results

docs.title: Proposal and weights
docs.text: Setting Default What it does mixture_alpha 0.1 Defensive mixture: fraction of each latent observable's theta draws from q(theta | x_i), the rest from q(theta | s_i); mixture_alpha * n_theta must be a whole number npe_ratio_ceiling 1.0 Clip the NPE ratio q(theta | s) / q(theta | x) at this per-star quantile (1.0 = no clip) imf_prior true Apply the IMF prior (Kroupa 2001) use_logg false Add the spectroscopic log g likelihood in stage 2

docs.title: Photometry, parallax and extinction
docs.text: Setting Default What it does bands ["G", "BP", "RP", "J", "H", "Ks"] Any subset of G, BP, RP, J, H, Ks that includes Ks extinction "F19" A name from extinction.EXTINCTION_LAWS, or a law object grey 0.0 Grey component added to every R_b of a built-in extinction law pseudo_mag_inflate true Inflate the pseudo absolute magnitude error by a Casagrande+21 A_K estimate (decima.ak) parallax_zero_point false Subtract the Lindegren+21 Gaia parallax zero-point (needs gaiadr3-zeropoint and the astrometry columns; see decima.io) parallax_snr_min 3.0 Parallaxes with parallax / error above this also enter the stage-2 (distance, extinction) fit directly

docs.title: Input errors and fills
docs.text: Setting Default What it does gaia_err_floor 0.02 [mag] floor on G, BP, RP errors twomass_err_floor 0.03 [mag] floor on J, H, Ks errors missing_err 0.5 [mag] error of a magnitude given without one (0: use the floor) alpha_fe_fill 0.0 [alpha/Fe] where the input has none alpha_fe_err_fill 0.2 Error in [alpha/Fe] when the input has none

docs.text: Setting Default What it does device "cpu" "cpu" or "cuda" stars_per_batch 100 Stars per stage-1 flow call

docs.title: Notes on some settings
docs.text:
• n_latent_x, n_theta, n_keep. n_latent_x is the Monte Carlo sample over the measurement noise, so change it first if you want more draws. The useful number of samples is the effective sample size, ess_frac × n_latent_x × n_theta; beyond it the n_keep samples are repeats.
  • seed. The same inputs, settings, chunk and seed give the same results. Chunk c of chunk stars is seeded seed + c * chunk, where stars are counted after rejected rows are dropped. CPU and CUDA draws differ.
  • mixture_alpha. mixture_alpha × n_theta must be a whole number (with n_theta = 10: 0, 0.1, 0.2, …). A bad value is refused with the allowed values.
  • extinction. One of "F19", "F19_TEFF", "SS2018", "WC2019", "none", or a law object (Python only). See Extinction laws.
  • pseudo_mag_inflate. See Pseudo-magnitude inflation.
  • parallax_snr_min. The exact parallax likelihood is used for every star; this only decides whether the parallax also enters the distance-extinction fit directly.
  • Errors. Spectroscopic errors (T_eff, [Fe/H], [α/Fe]) are used exactly as given: add a systematic term yourself if your survey needs one.
  • device. "cpu", "cuda" or "cuda:N". See Large catalogues.

docs.title: The parallax zero-point
docs.text:
With parallax_zero_point=True, DECIMA subtracts the Lindegren+21 zero-point from each parallax before using it. This needs:

  • the optional package: pip install 'decima-stars[zeropoint]';
  • the columns G, nu_eff_used_in_astrometry, pseudocolour, ecl_lat and astrometric_params_solved, with these Gaia archive names.

A star outside the recipe's validity keeps its parallax as given: G outside 6–21, a solution that is not 5- or 6-parameter, or a missing input. The summary column zero_point_applied records which stars were corrected.

docs.title: Not in the settings: how to run, not what to compute
docs.text:
Option Python Shell Default Worker processes run(..., workers=) --workers 1 Stars per checkpoint run(..., chunk=), infer(..., chunk=) --chunk 250 Summary file format run(..., summary_format=) --format fits Column mapping columns={...} --columns cols.json DECIMA's own names

Results do not depend on the number of workers. They do depend on chunk, because chunks are seeded by their first star, so a resumed run must use the same chunk size.
